message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated crime‑thriller releases from 2020 (in no particular order):

| Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A smart, low‑budget horror‑thriller that blends psychological suspense with a modern take on the classic monster myth. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a tense thriller, capturing the political unrest of 1969 with razor‑sharp dialogue and strong performances. |
| **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty crime caper featuring a star‑studded ensemble and a clever plot twist. |
| **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling, epic gangster saga that uses de‑scalation and time‑jumps to deliver a gripping, character‑driven thriller. |
| **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily Sullivan, David Wenham | A gritty, atmospheric thriller set in 19th‑century Tasmania, blending historical drama with tense, visceral action. |
| **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A psychological thriller that follows a man who becomes the target of a violent mob, exploring themes of paranoia and social media hysteria. |
| **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned thriller, with a strong focus on character motivations and a tense, unpredictable climax. |
| **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric thriller that weaves together multiple storylines in a small town, delivering a chilling, slow‑burn narrative. |
| **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson‑Cohen | A smart, low‑budget horror‑thriller that blends psychological suspense with a modern take on the classic monster myth. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul‑Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a tense thriller, capturing the political unrest of 1969 with razor‑sharp dialogue and strong performances. |

These films were praised for their tight storytelling, strong performances, and the way they kept audiences on the edge of their seats. If you’re looking for a mix of classic crime‑thriller tropes and fresh twists, any of these should hit the mark.
